reviews.evidence: The supplier gives pointwise chain, sum and bounded-bilinear product rules in real Banach spaces on open domains. The consumers are finite-dimensional real graphs on fixed strict open branches, hence instances of those spaces. Matrix composition/matrix-vector multiplication is bilinear and bounded by ||AB||<=||A||||B||; transpose is linear. The C2 closure Proof 2.1 applies chain rule to Dphi_j composed with the C1 parent tuple and product rule to its derivative-matrix product; continuity follows from the explicit C1 derivative-map hypotheses and continuous finite matrix multiplication, not from an unstated continuity conclusion of the supplier. Forward-over-reverse Proof 2.1 differentiates A^T*bar z_j by the same bounded-bilinear rule, using the forward tangent of the parent tuple. The prerequisite is real finite-dimensional differential calculus, not a Banach-manifold theorem or a Hessian-symmetry assumption.

reviews.evidence: Both consumer [F2]/[F5] uses match the supplier definition sup over measurable events, with values bounded by one; no signed-measure norm or missing factor 1/2 is used. The midpoint law and uniform law are probability measures on the same real Borel space, and the finite midpoint grid is measurable with probabilities one and zero. Box–Muller compares probability laws on the same R2 Borel space; all-input success makes its computed vector a deterministic finite-valued map, and the Gaussian-density law gives the finite support zero measure. Thus each support event attains TV=1, exactly as in the supplier convention. No Markov-chain stationarity, recurrence or ergodicity theorem is imported merely because that page homes the definition. The supplier adds no choice axiom; the consumers explicitly retain Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for their separate bit-product/Lebesgue-law suppliers.
